title: Artin–Schreier presentation and field-algebra dichotomy
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $E\subseteq F$ be fields of characteristic $p$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-pc-field-characteristic]. If $F/E$ is normal and separable of degree $p$, there are $z\in F\setminus E$ and $a\in E$ with $z^p-z=a$ and $F=E[z]$, and evaluation gives $E[T]/(T^p-T-a)\cong F$. Here normal means that every irreducible polynomial over $E$ having a root in $F$ splits in $F$, separable means that minimal polynomials have distinct roots, and degree is vector-space dimension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension, def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Polynomial rings and their quotient algebras have their usual coefficient structures [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Conversely, for every field $E$ of characteristic $p$ and $a\in E$, the algebra $E[T]/(T^p-T-a)$ is either a field, normal and separable of degree $p$ over $E$, or the product of $p$ copies of $E$; the latter case occurs exactly when $a=u^p-u$ for some $u\in E$.

source.place: Tag 09DY, lemma-Artin-Schreier, and section-Artin-Schreier immediately before it (the polynomial dichotomy); prime degree makes the Galois group cyclic of order p.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_E(F)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], $|G|=p$ and $F^G=E$. Apply [lem-sfb-prime-order-group-cyclic] to choose a generator $\sigma$. Its order is $p$: the distinct powers before its first return exhaust the cyclic group of $p$ elements. In particular $1,\sigma,\ldots,\sigma^{p-1}$ are distinct multiplicative characters on $F$.

Regard $\sigma$ as an $E$-linear endomorphism and put $N=\sigma-1$. In characteristic $p$, the intermediate binomial coefficients vanish, so $N^p=\sigma^p-1=0$. But $N^{p-1}\ne0$: expanding $(\sigma-1)^{p-1}$ would otherwise give a relation among the distinct characters $1,\sigma,\ldots,\sigma^{p-1}$ with leading coefficient $1$, contradicting [lem-per-monoid-characters-linear-independent]. Choose $w$ with $y=N^{p-1}w\ne0$. Since $Ny=0$, $y$ is fixed by the generator, hence by $G$, and therefore $y\in E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field].

source.place: Tag 09DY, lemma-Artin-Schreier, linear independence of characters; Tag 0CKL, lemma-independence-characters.

proof.text: Set $z=y^{-1}N^{p-2}w$; this is defined also for $p=2$, when $N^0=1$. As $y\in E$, $Nz=y^{-1}N^{p-1}w=1$, so $\sigma(z)=z+1$. Thus $z\notin E$, and $\sigma(z^p-z)=(z+1)^p-(z+1)=z^p-z$. The fixed-field statement gives $a=z^p-z\in E$. The $p$ elements $\sigma^i(z)=z+i\cdot1$ for $0\le i<p$ are distinct, since the characteristic is exactly $p$.

source.place: Tag 09DY, lemma-Artin-Schreier, explicit formula for z and final calculation.

proof.text: Write $f=T^p-T-a$. Evaluation at $z$ gives an $E$-algebra map $E[T]/(f)\to F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], its domain has basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{p-1}$. If a representative $q$ of degree $<p$ lies in its kernel, applying $\sigma^i$ to $q(z)=0$ gives $q(z+i)=0$ for all $0\le i<p$; hence $q=0$. Here the root bound follows by repeatedly dividing by $T-r$: at each distinct root the remaining quotient still vanishes at the other roots, so a nonzero polynomial with $p$ distinct roots has degree at least $p$. The map is injective between two $p$-dimensional $E$-spaces, hence bijective. Its image is $E[z]$, proving all the forward assertions.

source.place: Tag 09DY, lemma-Artin-Schreier, conclusion L=K[z]; quotient description via the monic basis.

proof.text: For the converse fix $E$ and $a$, and put $f=T^p-T-a$. Choose a root $b$ in an algebraic closure of $E$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. In characteristic $p$, $(x+t)^p=x^p+t^p$ by the binomial coefficients, and $(i\cdot1)^p=i\cdot1$ by induction on $i$. Hence the distinct $b+i\cdot1$, $0\le i<p$, are roots of $f$. Repeated division by these linear factors and comparison of degree and leading coefficient give $f=\prod_{i=0}^{p-1}(T-b-i\cdot1)$. Its roots are therefore exactly these translates. Put $L=E(b)$ and let $m$ be the minimal polynomial of $b$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. It divides $f$, because division by the monic $m$ leaves a polynomial of smaller degree vanishing at $b$. Write $f=mg$ in $E[T]$. In characteristic $p$ the derivative is $f'=p\,T^{p-1}-1=-1$, while $f'=m'g+mg'$; hence $m\cdot(-g')+m'\cdot(-g)=1$, so $m$ is coprime to its derivative, i.e. separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], and $b$ is separable over $E$. Thus $L/E$ is separable by [lem-trf-simple-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Tag 09I7, section-Artin-Schreier, paragraph preceding lemma-Artin-Schreier; Tags 09H1 and 09H9.

proof.text: All roots of $f$ lie in $L$, and they generate $L$ since one is $b$. Thus [lem-sfb-splitting-field-finite-normal] gives finite dimensionality and normality of $L/E$. Together with the preceding separability this permits [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]: its automorphism group $H$ has order $[L:E]$, and its fixed field is $E$. For $\tau\in H$, write $\tau(b)=b+c_\tau$ with $c_\tau\in\mathbf F_p$, using the explicit root list of step 5. Since every automorphism fixes the prime field, $c_{\tau\rho}=c_\tau+c_\rho$. This homomorphism is injective, since fixing $b$ fixes the generated field $L$.

source.place: Tag 09I7, section-Artin-Schreier, injection of the Galois group into Z/pZ; Tags 09HU, 09I1, 09DW.

proof.text: If $b\notin E$, the fixed-field result in step 6 supplies $\tau$ moving $b$. Its nonzero $c_\tau\in\mathbf F_p$ has $p$ distinct multiples: equality of two would give $(i-j)c_\tau=0$, impossible for $0<|i-j|<p$. The powers of $\tau$ therefore give $p$ distinct elements of $H$; injectivity into the $p$-element prime field gives $|H|=p$. Consequently $[L:E]=p$. Evaluation $E[T]/(f)\to L$ is injective by exactly the degree/root argument of step 4, now using the $p$ conjugates of $b$ supplied by powers of $\tau$. The monic basis [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] and equality of dimensions make it an isomorphism. This is the field case, with normality and separability already established.

source.place: Tag 09I7, section-Artin-Schreier, order of the translation group, with the quotient argument written out.

proof.text: If $b=u\in E$, the roots $r_i=u+i\cdot1$ all lie in $E$. Evaluation gives $E[T]/(f)\to E^p$. Its inverse as a vector-space map sends $(v_i)_i$ to the class of $\sum_i v_i\prod_{j\ne i}(T-r_j)/(r_i-r_j)$. The denominators are nonzero; evaluating at $r_k$ gives $v_k$. Injectivity follows from the root bound and the degree-$<p$ representatives supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. Thus evaluation is a bijective algebra homomorphism, so an algebra isomorphism. A root $u\in E$ is exactly an equation $a=u^p-u$. Conversely an algebra isomorphism with $E^p$ followed by any coordinate projection sends the class of $T$ to such a root $u$. The two cases are exclusive since $p\ge2$ and $E^p$ has nonzero zero divisors.

source.place: Tag 09I7, section-Artin-Schreier, split-root case; explicit interpolation inverse rather than an implicit Chinese remainder theorem.
